The LOCO ablation results explain the behaviors visually identified in the multi-variable trajectories. 

*   **Archetype 1:** The top two driving features are exclusively moisture-related (`d_humidity_delta` and `humidity_delta`). The complete absence of power features driving this score confirms the model isolated this state based purely on a transient, unpowered humidity disturbance.
*   **Archetype 2:** Electrical power (`dw_power`) acts as the primary trigger, followed immediately by thermal and energy derivatives. This validates the visual assessment of a commanded system startup.
*   **Archetype 3:** The anomaly score is driven by extreme deviations in thermal derivatives and margins (e.g., `d_t_supply_15m`, `d_supply_margin`). Crucially, power features do not appear in the top drivers. This mathematical decoupling confirms an unmetered thermal bleed, verifying that heat is entering the system externally.
*   **Archetype 4:** Dominated by a combination of collapsing margins (`d_supply_margin`, `displacement_return_margin`) and temperature short-term derivatives. This again suggests a hard system shutdown.

### Forensic Ledger

Once the optimal number of clusters is validated and the medoids are extracted, the next step is to lock in the baseline. The `commit_ledger()` method finalizes this state by mapping every isolated anomaly in the historical data to its closest archetype (medoid) based on the Hamming distance derived from the isolation forest.

```{r}
#| label: commit-ledger
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Show Ledger Commit"
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Lock the baseline and map all historical anomalies
engine_baseline <- commit_ledger(engine_baseline)

# Extract the flat dataframe for analysis
baseline_ledger <- get_ledger(engine_baseline)
head(baseline_ledger[,1:4], 10)
```

Only the first four columns are displayed above, but the ledger also contains all target and context variables for all anomalies that have a score above the chosen threshold. 

This means that we can summarize the obtained clusters by using the ledger as follows.

```{r}
#| label: ledger-summary
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: show
#| code-summary: "Summarize Ledger"
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

# Generate a high-level operational summary of the baseline period
ledger_summary <- baseline_ledger |>
  group_by(anomaly_cluster) |>
  summarise(
    Total_Occurrences = n(),
    First_Seen = min(as.Date(timestamp)),
    Last_Seen = max(as.Date(timestamp)),
    Median_Score = round(median(anomaly_score), 3),
    Max_Distance = round(max(topological_distance), 3)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Total_Occurrences))

kable(ledger_summary, caption = "Summary of historical anomaly archetypes.")
```

`Max_Distance` represents the *radius* of the cluster. It measures the forest-based distance between the archetype (medoid, distance = 0) and the furthest point that belongs to that cluster.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Extract the fully scored timeline using the new accessor
full_scored_data <- get_scored_time_course(engine_baseline)

# 2. Run Spearman's Rank Correlation Test
# H0: No monotonic trend between time and anomaly score
# HA: Anomaly scores monotonically increase (or decrease) over time
trend_test <- cor.test(
  as.numeric(full_scored_data$timestamp), 
  full_scored_data$anomaly_score, 
  method = "spearman", 
  exact = FALSE
)

cat("Spearman Rank Correlation (rho):", round(trend_test$estimate, 4), "\n")
cat("p-value:", signif(trend_test$p.value, 4), "\n")

if(trend_test$p.value < 0.05 && trend_test$estimate > 0) {
  cat("Verdict: Statistically significant upward creep detected.\n")
} else {
  cat("Verdict: No significant continuous upward trend.\n")
}

# 3. Visualize the un-thresholded scores to see the "sub-clinical" behavior
ggplot(full_scored_data, aes(x = timestamp, y = anomaly_score)) +
  # Use high transparency since there are tens of thousands of points
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, size = 0.5, color = "grey50") +
  # GAM smoother to capture non-linear creeps over time
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "cs"), 
              color = "darkred", linewidth = 1.2, se = TRUE) +
  # Add our T=0.6 threshold line for context
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Full-Spectrum Anomaly Score Trend",
    subtitle = "Testing for 'sub-clinical' mechanical degradation via Spearman's rho",
    x = "Timeline",
    y = "Raw Isolation Forest Score"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: eda-full-routing
#| echo: true
#| message: true
#| warning: false

# Helper function to route the entire timeline to the committed medoids
route_full_timeline <- function(engine, max_distance = 0.45) {
  
  # 1. Get full scored data and raw features
  full_data <- get_scored_time_course(engine)
  features <- engine@feature_matrix
  medoid_sigs <- engine@baseline_signatures
  
  k <- nrow(medoid_sigs)
  n_trees <- ncol(medoid_sigs)
  
  message("Extracting terminal nodes for the entire dataset...")
  # O(N) complexity - very fast
  full_sigs <- stats::predict(engine@model, features, type = "tree_num")
  
  message("Computing topological distances to medoids...")
  # Initialize distance matrix (N x k)
  dist_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(full_data), ncol = k)
  colnames(dist_mat) <- rownames(medoid_sigs)
  
  for (i in 1:k) {
    # Vectorized Hamming distance: compare all N points to medoid i
    disagreements <- colSums(t(full_sigs) != medoid_sigs[i, ])
    dist_mat[, i] <- disagreements / n_trees
  }
  
  # 2. Find the closest medoid for each point
  closest_idx <- max.col(-dist_mat, ties.method = "first")
  min_dists <- dist_mat[cbind(1:nrow(dist_mat), closest_idx)]
  
  # 3. Assign labels and distances
  full_data$closest_archetype <- colnames(dist_mat)[closest_idx]
  full_data$distance_to_archetype <- min_dists
  
  # 4. Enforce the "Other/Normal" bucket
  full_data$archetype_bucket <- ifelse(
    full_data$distance_to_archetype > max_distance,
    "Background Noise",
    full_data$closest_archetype
  )
  
  return(full_data)
}

# --- Execution ---

# 1. Route the timeline
routed_timeline <- route_full_timeline(engine_baseline, max_distance = 0.45)

# 2. Quick summary of the bucketing
table(routed_timeline$archetype_bucket)

# 3. Plot the sub-clinical creep, faceted by Archetype
library(ggplot2)

# Filter out background noise so we only look at points topologically related to our faults
creeping_faults <- subset(routed_timeline, archetype_bucket != "Background Noise")

ggplot(creeping_faults, aes(x = timestamp, y = anomaly_score, color = archetype_bucket)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "cs"), 
              color = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~archetype_bucket, ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo", guide = "none") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Sub-Clinical Anomaly Creep by Archetype",
    subtitle = "Tracking specific mechanical states before they breach the threshold",
    x = "Timeline",
    y = "Anomaly Score"
  ) +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0"))
```

```{r}
#| label: eda-empirical-radii
#| echo: true
#| message: true
#| warning: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Extract and align the Empirical Radii from the baseline ledger
empirical_radii <- baseline_ledger |>
  group_by(anomaly_cluster) |>
  summarise(event_horizon = max(topological_distance)) |>
  # Fix the naming mismatch between extract_medoids and commit_ledger
  mutate(anomaly_cluster = gsub("_", " ", anomaly_cluster)) |> 
  tibble::deframe() # Converts to a named numeric vector

cat("Calculated Empirical Radii (Event Horizons):\n")
print(round(empirical_radii, 3))

# 2. Re-write the routing function to use the dynamic radii
route_timeline_empirically <- function(engine, radii) {
  
  full_data <- get_scored_time_course(engine)
  features <- engine@feature_matrix
  medoid_sigs <- engine@baseline_signatures
  
  k <- nrow(medoid_sigs)
  n_trees <- ncol(medoid_sigs)
  
  full_sigs <- stats::predict(engine@model, features, type = "tree_num")
  
  dist_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(full_data), ncol = k)
  colnames(dist_mat) <- rownames(medoid_sigs)
  
  for (i in 1:k) {
    disagreements <- colSums(t(full_sigs) != medoid_sigs[i, ])
    dist_mat[, i] <- disagreements / n_trees
  }
  
  # Find closest medoid and its distance
  closest_idx <- max.col(-dist_mat, ties.method = "first")
  closest_clusters <- colnames(dist_mat)[closest_idx]
  min_dists <- dist_mat[cbind(1:nrow(dist_mat), closest_idx)]
  
  full_data$closest_archetype <- closest_clusters
  full_data$distance_to_archetype <- min_dists
  
  # 3. Apply the specific empirical radius for each point's closest cluster
  point_specific_radii <- radii[closest_clusters]
  
  full_data$archetype_bucket <- ifelse(
    min_dists <= point_specific_radii,
    closest_clusters,
    "Background Noise"
  )
  
  return(full_data)
}

# Execute the new routing
routed_empirical <- route_timeline_empirically(engine_baseline, empirical_radii)

# Check how the bucketing adjusted based on the true topological shapes
cat("\nRouting Distribution using Empirical Radii:\n")
print(table(routed_empirical$archetype_bucket))

# Plot the creeping faults again with the true boundaries
creeping_empirical <- subset(routed_empirical, archetype_bucket != "Background Noise")

ggplot(creeping_empirical, aes(x = timestamp, y = anomaly_score, color = archetype_bucket)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "cs"), 
              color = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~archetype_bucket, ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo", guide = "none") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Sub-Clinical Anomaly Creep (Empirical Radii)",
    subtitle = "Archetypes bounded strictly by their historical maximum topological variance",
    x = "Timeline",
    y = "Anomaly Score"
  ) +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0"))
```

```{r}
  min_N = 30, 
  nb_steps = 61,
  min_k = 2,
  max_k = 10
)

plot_base <- res_base |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(N_Anomalies, Opt_k, Hartigans_D, Global_LID), 
    names_to = "Metric", 
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |>
  mutate(Metric = factor(Metric, levels = c("N_Anomalies", "Hartigans_D", "Global_LID", "Opt_k")))

max_dip_base <- plot_base |>
  filter(Metric == "Hartigans_D") |>
  filter(Value == max(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  slice(1)

# Isolate the minimum LID coordinate for highlighting
min_lid_base <- plot_base |>
  filter(Metric == "Global_LID") |>
  filter(Value == min(Value, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  slice(1)

ggplot(plot_base, aes(x = Threshold, y = Value, color = Metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_point(data = max_dip_base, fill = "gold", color = "red", size = 4, shape = 21, stroke = 1.2) +
  # Highlight the minimum Global_LID point
  geom_point(data = min_lid_base, fill = "gold", color = "red", size = 4, shape = 21, stroke = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~Metric, 
    scales = "free_y", 
    ncol = 1,
    labeller = as_labeller(c(
      N_Anomalies = "Number of Anomalies (N)",
      Hartigans_D = "Cluster Effect Size (Hartigan's Dip Statistic)", 
      Global_LID = "Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID)",
      Opt_k = "Optimal Clusters (k)"
    ))
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "N_Anomalies" = "#0072B2", 
    "Hartigans_D" = "#009E73", 
    "Global_LID" = "#CC79A7", 
    "Opt_k" = "#D55E00"
  )) +
  # Use dynamic breaks since threshold values are dynamically extracted from N
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 10) +
  labs(
    title = "Topological Validation: Baseline Configuration",
    subtitle = "Target Variables: delta_t, delta_rh, delta_t_deriv_15m",
    x = "Anomaly Threshold",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: estimate-healthy-lid
#| echo: true

# 1. Extract Full System State
features <- engine_base@feature_matrix
hyps <- engine_base@hyperparameters
ntrees <- hyps$ntrees
actual_size <- min(hyps$sample_size, nrow(features))

# Train global model to predict scores and isolate "normal" data
global_model <- suppressWarnings(
  isotree::isolation.forest(features, ntrees = ntrees, sample_size = actual_size, missing_action = "fail")
)
global_scores <- stats::predict(global_model, features)

# Define "Healthy" as the lowest 50% of anomaly scores
threshold_healthy <- median(global_scores)
healthy_idx <- which(global_scores <= threshold_healthy)

# 2. Find Valid Contiguous Blocks (N = 30)
# We need 30 sequential time steps that are ALL classified as healthy
block_size <- 30
valid_starts <- c()

max_start <- nrow(features) - block_size + 1
for (i in 1:max_start) {
  if (all((i:(i + block_size - 1)) %in% healthy_idx)) {
    valid_starts <- c(valid_starts, i)
  }
}

if (length(valid_starts) == 0) {
  stop("No contiguous healthy blocks found! Adjust the health threshold.")
}

message(sprintf("Found %d valid contiguous healthy blocks of size %d.", length(valid_starts), block_size))

# 3. Monte Carlo: Sample blocks and compute local LID
iterations <- 200
k_neighbors <- 5
healthy_lids <- numeric(iterations)

set.seed(42)
sampled_starts <- sample(valid_starts, iterations, replace = TRUE)

for (i in seq_along(sampled_starts)) {
  start_idx <- sampled_starts[i]
  block_idx <- start_idx:(start_idx + block_size - 1)
  block_features <- features[block_idx, ]
  
  # Build local Isolation Forest geometry to match the anomaly pipeline exactly
  iso_model <- suppressWarnings(
    isotree::isolation.forest(block_features, ntrees = ntrees, sample_size = block_size, missing_action = "fail")
  )
  d_obj <- stats::predict(iso_model, block_features, type = "dist")
  d_mat <- as.matrix(d_obj)
  
  # Compute Global LID for this healthy block
  # We pass a dummy cluster label since we only care about the Global_LID return value
  lid_res <- compute_lid_profile(d_mat, cluster_labels = rep(1, block_size), k = k_neighbors)
  healthy_lids[i] <- lid_res$Global_LID
}

mean_healthy_lid <- mean(healthy_lids, na.rm = TRUE)
quantiles <- stats::quantile(healthy_lids, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

message(sprintf("\n--- Healthy Control Baseline (N=%d) ---", block_size))
message(sprintf("Mean Healthy LID: %.3f", mean_healthy_lid))
message(sprintf("Empirical 95%% Interval: [%.3f, %.3f]", quantiles[1], quantiles[2]))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-extreme-medoids

#| message: false

#| fig-height: 10

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# 1. DYNAMICALLY TARGET THE EXACT PEAK FROM THE STABILITY SWEEP
# Pull the exact threshold where Hartigan's D reached its maximum in res_base
th_extreme <- res_base$Threshold[which.max(res_base$Hartigans_D)]

message(sprintf("Targeting Peak Threshold (T = %.4f)...", th_extreme))

# 2. EXTRACT AND CLUSTER USING S4 API
# The fixed seed guarantees we perfectly recreate the sweep's topology
engine_extreme <- suppressMessages(extract_anomalies(engine_base, threshold = th_extreme))
engine_extreme <- suppressMessages(compute_distances(engine_extreme))
engine_extreme <- suppressMessages(calibrate(engine_extreme, min_k = 2, max_k = 2))
engine_extreme <- suppressMessages(extract_medoids(engine_extreme, k = 2))

# 3. EXTRACT AND WRANGLE DYNAMIC WINDOWS
message("Formatting +/- 2 hour medoid windows for k=2...")
raw_medoids <- get_medoids(engine_extreme)

# Dynamically pull valid columns from the active schema to prevent silent drops
schema <- get_features(engine_extreme)
plot_vars <- intersect(
  c(schema$context_variables, schema$target_variables), 
  colnames(raw_medoids)
)

# Helper to automatically format variable names for the plot labels
format_var_name <- function(x) {
  str_to_title(str_replace_all(str_replace_all(x, "_15m", ""), "_", " "))
}

plot_data <- raw_medoids %>%
  mutate(
    Relative_Time = as.numeric(difftime(timestamp, medoid_timestamp, units = "hours")),
    Archetype = str_replace(cluster, "Cluster", "Archetype")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(plot_vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable_Clean = factor(Variable, levels = plot_vars, labels = sapply(plot_vars, format_var_name)),
    Archetype_Label = case_when(
      Archetype == "Archetype 1" ~ "1: Terminal Mode A",
      Archetype == "Archetype 2" ~ "2: Terminal Mode B",
      TRUE ~ Archetype
    )
  )

# 4. VISUALIZATION MATRIX
fig_extreme <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Relative_Time, y = Value, color = Variable_Clean)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", alpha = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(Variable_Clean ~ Archetype_Label, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo") + 
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Multivariate Trajectories of Terminal HVAC Faults (T=%.4f)", th_extreme),
    subtitle = "Features displayed reflect the active YAML schema of the target engine.",
    x = "Relative Time from Structural Break (Hours)",
    y = "Telemetry Value"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    strip.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, angle = 270), 
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0", color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(0, "pt"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey80", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5)
  )

print(fig_extreme)
```
